title.narrative: COVID-19: Vaccine Support under the Asia Pacific Vaccine Access Facility

description.narrative:
The project is aligned with the following impacts: (i) stabilize the situation and save lives; and (ii) spread, morbidity, and mortality of COVID-19 reduced and confidence of citizens restored. The project outcome is that the target populations per the NVDP are vaccinated against COVID-19.
Output 1. COVID-19 vaccine procured and delivered to designated points. The project will finance procurement and delivery of vaccines through bilateral deals between the government and manufacturers and/or through the COVAX Facility. Procurement through bilateral deals with other countries will be considered, subject to due diligence and necessary approvals. To vaccinate an estimated 0.3 million persons, 0.7 million doses of COVID-19 vaccines (assuming 10% adjustment for wastage) will be delivered to regional warehouses according to the NVDP. The expenditure items under the RRC will include (i) vaccines that meet any of the eligibility requirements of the APVAX policy, including advance payments; (ii) international logistics and related services required to transport vaccines from the place of purchase to regional warehouses; and (iii) ancillary items such as syringes, safety boxes, and other items required to administer the vaccines. The NCDC will be responsible for transporting the vaccine from the regional warehouses to the vaccine administration sites. Before the disbursement of the loan proceeds, MOILHSA shall submit to ADB purchase agreements for the vaccines that comply with APVAX policy requirements.
Output 2. Vaccine program implementation capacity strengthened. Under the PIC, the project will support activities that will strengthen (i) the project implementation unit (PIU) under the MOILHSA to help implement and monitor the COVID-19 vaccination program; and (ii) carry out gender mainstreaming activities, which include approving updated budget and guidelines for mobile teams to reach marginalized groups, including women. Additional staff will be hired under the project to augment PIU capacity.

Output: COVID-19 vaccine procured and delivered to designated points Indicator: At least 0.2 million doses of COVID-19 vaccine delivered to regional vaccine stores (with retroactive financing) Progress/Status: In total 500,000 doses of vaccines were procured from Sinopharm by the contract, part of which (approx. 235,000) was retroactively financed by the ADB.

Output: Vaccine program implementation capacity strengthened Indicator: 80% of trainees (at least 40% women) demonstrated gender-sensitive skills in COVID-19 vaccine administration Progress/Status: Completed
Gender sensitivity training module was developed by gender and social development specialist of the project implementing unit (PIU). Goal of the developed project is to gather rather comprehensive and at the same time, user-friendly materials that will help trainer to achieve his/her mission effectively, at the same time helping training participants in raising awareness on gender and gender sensitivity.
The developed training program includes, as theoretical portion on gender, gender roles and stereotypes, gender equality and gender policy, discrimination and violence against women, gender aspects of vaccination, opportunities to strengthen the involvement of women and vulnerable groups in the vaccination process, in the process of providing vaccination services to women and vulnerable groups. Information on ways to prevent discrimination based on gender/sexuality, as well as practical exercises, video materials and pre- and post-tests to assess gender sensitivity among training participants. Gender sensitivity training provides educational information related to the following issues: 1. Definition of Basic Concepts • The notion of Gender • What is sex? What are the core differences between Sex and Gender? • The notion of Gender equality
2. Gender Relations and Characteristics • The roles of Gender and Gender functions • Gender-related norms and stereotypes • Gender relation models • Labor distribution and Double Load
3. Gender Equality • Gender equality and human rights • Institutional mechanisms for Gender equality • Local and international commitments of gender equality • Gender-based discrimination • Gender-based discrimination in labor relations
4. Gender-Based Violence • What is gender-based violence? • Forms and types of gender-based violence • Social environment and gender-based violence • Legal aspects of gender-based violence: internal legislative-legal analysis; preventive mechanisms • How to protect own rights, responsibility, obligations, and skillset required for action
5. Gender Mainstreaming • Idea of mainstreaming • Importance of implementation of gender mainstreaming in practice
6. COVID-19 Impact on Gender Aspects • Assessment of risks caused by pandemic • Overview and discussion of current studies and statistics • SEA/SH complaint mechanisms After the development of the training module, the cycle of gender sensitivity trainings started in April of 2022 and will continue till October 2023.
Within the given timeframe, 17 Gender sensitivity trainings were conducted with medical professionals working at large immunization medical facilities in Tbilisi and regions. Members of the project implementing unit (PIU) also attended gender sensitivity trainings. Trainings were conducted in the physical environment. In total, more than 298 health professionals attended trainings. 90% of the training participants were women The success of gender sensitivity training can be considered that between the results of pre and post-tests, in different medical institutions, an increase of at least 10% and at most 50% is recorded. Overall, the average gender sensitivity increased to 100% at the end of each training session.
